title: Approval Token Generation
description: Produces exact human approval commands with gate, approval request ID, scope hash short, and UTC expiry for gated actions. Generation creates a request for authority; it does not create or grant authority.
intent: Generate a deterministic, non-secret gate-approval-request artifact that binds gate, approval_request_id, 16-hex scope_hash_short, target, actor, and UTC expiry, failing closed on missing, ambiguous, stale, or non-approval-boundary inputs. The emitted approval_command follows the canonical grammar APPROVE <GATE_SHORT> <approval_request_id> <scope_hash_short:16hex> <expires_at_utc>.
outcome: gate-approval-request artifact containing approval_request_id, task_id, repository, gate, action, scope bindings (base_sha, head_sha, branch, pr_number, environment), scope_hash, scope_hash_short, actor_target, issued_at, expires_at, non-secret 64-hex approval_token (integrity evidence only, never in the human command), canonical approval_command, request_digest (sha256), reason_codes, and authority_granted=false.
constraints: The evaluator is pure and deterministic for the same semantic inputs; issued_at/expires_at are binding inputs to the digest, not diagnostic.

Equivalent normalized semantic inputs must produce the same approval_token, approval_command, and request_digest; material changes to task, repository, gate, action, base_sha, head_sha, scope_hash, actor, or expiry must change/invalidate prior evidence.
Generation must never grant G2, G4, G5, G6, merge, deploy, release, credential, migration, or production-data authority; authority_granted must be false.

The human approval_command must bind gate_short, approval_request_id, 16-hex scope_hash_short, and second-precision UTC expiry exactly per the canonical grammar; the 64-hex approval_token is integrity evidence only and must never appear in the human command.
Material drift in scope_hash, base_sha, head_sha, or actor invalidates the prior token evidence and requires regeneration.
exclusions: Granting or validating human approval or gate transition authority.
Performing a gate transition, merge, deploy, release, migration, or production-data operation.
Reading or mutating repositories, Jira, GitHub, branches, worktrees, PRs, deployments, releases, credentials, or production data.
Consumed-token state tracking or replay consumption; that belongs to consumer node gate_authority.approval-command-validation (SCRUM-309).
entry_guards: task_id, repository, gate, action, scope_identity (with scope_hash, base_sha, head_sha), actor_target.id, issued_at, expires_at are available

reason_codes.APPROVAL_REQUEST_GENERATED: A deterministic gate-approval-request artifact was produced; authority is not granted.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_INPUT_INVALID: task_id, repository, gate, action, scope_identity, actor_target.id, or expiry inputs are structurally invalid.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_BOUNDARY_NOT_REQUESTED: The authority boundary decision does not require approval.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_GATE_ACTION_MISMATCH: The requested action does not match the boundary decision's requested_action.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_BINDING_REQUIRED: A required scope binding (base_sha, head_sha, branch, pr_number, environment) is absent or malformed.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_EXPIRY_INVALID: Expiry is absent, not after issuance, or not second-precision UTC.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_G5_MANUAL_SCOPE_REQUIRED: A G5 gate request lacks a manual environment binding.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_G6_NOT_APPLICABLE: A G6 gate request is made without applicable production scope.
reason_codes.APPROVAL_REDACTION_REQUIRED: A derived identifier or token failed the non-secret canonical format contract.
